scope: Independent check of the literature sources cited by the validation note. The implementation was written without access to the paper hosts; this record describes what the reviewer read and found. No numerical run was performed for this check.

implementation_reviewed.description: off-axis science implementation at development revision 516aff0 (before publication)

sources.title: The Anisoplanatic Point Spread Function in Adaptive Optics
sources.access: Relevant sections of full text read in the independent review.

locators.finding: The factorization neglects cross terms with guide-star correction errors. The guide-star OTF becomes the diffraction reference under ideal on-axis correction.
Eq. 8 expresses shear in pupil-radius units. In metres at zenith the shear is s = h theta. Eq. 12 contains two positive doubled terms and the two negative displaced-baseline terms.
Figure 1 illustrates directional dependence. Figure 2 uses a 5 m telescope and a 2.12 micrometre Strehl curve under ideal guide-star correction.

sources.comparison: For a stationary layer with phase structure function D, the four-point form is 2D(rho) + 2D(s) - D(rho+s) - D(rho-s). It vanishes at either zero baseline or zero shear. Substituting a finite-outer-scale von Karman structure function adapts the published Kolmogorov calculation.

sources.title: Anisoplanatism in adaptive optics
sources.access: Publisher abstract read in the independent review. Full-text equations not used.
sources.finding: The exponential angular factor characterizes the imaging OTF at high spatial frequencies. The separate large-aperture statement concerns transmitter antenna gain. The abstract does not supply a universal finite-aperture imaging Strehl acceptance test.

open_scientific_issue.observation: The band-limit perturbation to Strehl is evaluated only over lag indices -8 through +8 in each axis. All other pupil-autocorrelation lags retain the continuous prediction. The acceptance comparison uses the continuous Strehl.
open_scientific_issue.action: Use the full weighted lag support or bound the omitted contribution before asserting a global effect below 1e-6. Otherwise explicitly report the subtotal and leave the total undetermined. This is reference-side work and does not itself require a new closed-loop trajectory.
